beats.brief_ref: §2 AG finding (verified: AG report p. 2 and p. 4)
beats.narration_text: The Massachusetts Attorney General found that residential customers on competitive supply paid seven hundred thirty-eight point seven million dollars more than basic service over the last decade. Suppliers charging ten to thirty percent above basic service account for more than half of those losses. Markups that size are hard to spot on a bill.

beats.narration_text: Electricity Supplier Check will read a Massachusetts electric bill and tell you exactly how much more, or less, you paid than basic service, with the math shown. It will be a Python repository with the agent, a dated rate table where every row cites its tariff, constructed test bills with known answers, and an evaluation report.

beats.narration_text: The other reader is a hiring manager for my target role: AI engineer for agentic systems, ideally at an energy company. In their first sixty seconds, they'll open the project's GitHub repository and its evaluation report. For every test bill, it will show whether each number in Claude's explanation matches a number the Python calculator produced, and they can rerun the tests themselves.

beats.brief_ref: §2 alternatives; 'will save a household the work of…'
beats.narration_text: I looked at two real alternatives. Energy Switch Massachusetts helps you shop for a new supplier, but doesn't read your bill or tell you what you've already paid extra. Some towns' energy coaches check whether you're on competitive supply, but that needs a person, and it is not instant. Mine will save a household the work of finding the right published rate, matching it to the billing period, and doing the math.

beats.brief_ref: §4; Will exist list; Stack header (Claude Code builds it and is how the agent calls Claude; no paid API calls)
beats.narration_text: Claude will read the bill into a fixed schema, and code will check it. Python will do all the math: match the billing period to a dated rate table, prorate across rate changes, and compute the difference. Then Claude will explain the result, and a verifier will reject any number that code didn't compute. I'll build it in Python and py-test with Claude Code, and the agent will call Claude through Claude Code too, with no paid API calls.

beats.brief_ref: §4 What does it prove about me?
beats.narration_text: Building it will show the skills this course teaches: prompt contracts, verification kept separate from generation, source grounding, a bounded agent loop with retries, and held-out evaluation. The evidence will be my test suite, constructed bills with planted traps, and traces of drafts the verifier rejected. A reviewer could fairly conclude I can pull exact, auditable numbers out of messy documents without letting the model invent any.
